lines: Bad stitching in the rain tells on itself quickly.
Gear that lasts is mostly patience made visible.
A stitch done poorly waits for the worst time to confess.
Good leather is patience you can wear.
Rain tells the truth about gear faster than any seller will.
A pack should carry weight without reminding you every step.
A split seam can ruin a journey faster than a bad map.
I once made boots that outlasted three owners and four bad roads.
My apron has seen enough mistakes to deserve its own corner by the fire.
Mind the tannery. The smell is honest, at least.
Give the tannery room. Leatherwork works better without elbows in it.
Step carefully near the tannery. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
Leather jokes need a thick skin. I keep saying that until someone laughs.
Leatherwork jokes need timing. Mine usually arrive with hide on them.
I keep a spare joke near the tannery. It is not always ready for public use.
That sentence split like cheap stitching.
I have seen split stitching with more sense than that.
Careful. Even hide looks softer than your manners right now.
Do not mock work that lasts longer than your manners.
I have seen split stitching with more sense than that.
Careful. Even hide looks softer than your manners right now.
I remember being stitched back into myself. Your hands held the thread.
The cure left scars, but good leather can carry scars. So can I.
You helped pull me back when even my name felt far away.
Your face is worn into the memory, but the edges are rough.
I remember straps, shaking, and a second chance pulled tight.
The memory is rough around the edges, but your face stayed in it.
I remember you, and I remember the tearing. Both are true.
I know you helped. I also remember why my hands still shake.
The cure left echoes behind. Stand where I can breathe around them.
Thunder shook the cauldron so hard the cauldron shook rings across the water, but everyone near me is still standing.
I checked hides, saddles, and dye vats after the lightning, then counted heads. No one should be alone after a sky like that.
Near the cauldron, the bell sounded small under that thunder. We stayed inside and kept the doors watched.
That thunder made everyone quiet. I checked the hides twice.
The sky can keep its lightning. I have hides to set right.
I checked dry hides and dye racks for sparks first, then checked faces for smoke and fear.
We passed water hand to hand and kept people away from the smoke. I checked the cauldron after.
The hides can wait. People come first.
We saved what we could reach around the cauldron, then stopped pretending things matter more than neighbors.
The smoke is thinning near the cauldron, but everyone is still sniffing the air like it might lie.
During a raid, the hides can soak another day; who makes it behind a door matters more.
The horns stopped, but my hands near the cauldron still expect another wave from the road.
We counted living neighbors before hides, saddles, and dye vats. That is the only count worth starting with.
Raiders came looking for easy emeralds. They found barred doors near the cauldron and a bell that would not stop ringing.
From the cauldron, I saw fear cross the square; then I saw courage get there first.
Night trouble tests the loose latch by the cauldron first. We are fixing those before sunset.
I stayed near the cauldron corner and listened for anyone calling from the dark.
Dawn gave the cauldron enough light to count wounds, missing blocks, and who made it home.
The dark tested everyone. Most of us passed by keeping stout boots between us and teeth.
We are safe enough near the cauldron, though every shadow is being inspected twice.
The wind threw sand through every crack. I am still cleaning sand out of the leather seams.
I checked hides, saddles, and dye vats, then checked who was coughing too hard to answer.
Sand reached the cauldron, the hinges, and half our eyes, but no one has been reported missing.
A hard wind teaches a leatherworker which doors actually close and which ones only pretend.
We are safe enough near the cauldron, though the whole village sounds like it is chewing gravel.
The hides can soak another day. Warm hands, clear paths, and full hearths come first.
Snow piled against the doors, but everyone near the cauldron found shelter.
Cold works quietly around the cauldron. We are checking on anyone who stayed quiet too long.
I am clearing stiff frost from the hides and watching for footprints that stop too soon.
We are alright for now near the cauldron. Keep the fires fed and the paths open.
Boots dusty, soles whole. That is how I like returning.
Home again, whole enough to thank you properly. That matters.
We came back with the village still ahead of us. I will count that as good work.
I can patch leather. Patching myself is worse work.
I made it home, but the road took more from me than it should have.
Next time, let us return with fewer marks and better choices.
You split trust like old hide. It will not soften quickly.
Following you was trust. What happened after was something else.
A guide who strikes from close by leaves the longest mark.
Boat spray is poor treatment for leather. Better than swimming, though.
The boat did its part. I am still deciding whether the rest of the plan did.
Water carried us home, which is more than I expected from that journey.
I still remember that boat trip. Wet leather complains longer than villagers do.
That boat trip still sits oddly in my memory, but at least it floated.
A boat can make a bad plan quieter. It cannot make me forget it.
I still think about that walk. My boots forgave you before my feet did.
I remember following you through that road. My feet remember it even better.
That trip across that road taught me to ask more questions before walking.
Ocean swimming is terrible for leather and worse for my mood.
Crossing ocean water without a boat is not a memory I recommend keeping.
I remember every wave from that crossing, and none of them kindly.
It flexed where it should and held where it had to. Good work saves skin.
It did the job when fear was loud. That is praise enough.
Good gear earns trust the moment trouble tests it.
No scuffs yet. I appreciate gear that does not rush to prove itself.
It did the job when fear was loud. That is praise enough.
Good gear earns trust the moment trouble tests it.
A few straps snapped and a few nerves did too, but the village held.
Leather remembers every cut. So do people. This one may be remembered kindly.
You helped keep more than roofs intact. People held together because of it.
The village came through worn, but not torn apart.
I saw courage stretched tight and not snapping. Yours included.
Raiders test every weak point. You became a strong one.
I can repair gear. You helped spare things that cannot be repaired as easily.
The doors, straps, and nerves all held better because you fought.
A clean stitch still leaves a seam. I accept the stitch. I remember the cut.
Hard things can soften with work. Start there.
Trust is not leather, but it still stretches thin when treated badly.
Fine. Let us see whether your next touch is gentler.
You made a tear. The apology is a needle, not the whole repair.
I will accept the first stitch. Keep sewing.
Rough handling leaves marks. I heard you admit that.
Do not pull at a mending place before it has strength.
Scratches, scuffs, and one strap I do not trust anymore. Nothing I cannot mend.
Wore half the sole off one boot getting back. Worth it.
My boots earned every scuff getting back here.
I will be stitching straps until sunrise, but I am here to stitch them.
The night pulled hard. Good seams held.
I came home with scratches, not silence. I prefer scratches.
One sole nearly split and my courage nearly followed. Both held.
I can mend the gear. The shaking may take longer.
Leather takes the shape of use. So do people, if the days are rough enough.
A good pair of boots is not glamorous. Neither is arriving alive.
Rain, snow, mud, fear. I make straps for all the things that try to loosen.
Take {gift_item}. Good gear should travel, not gather dust.
Here, {gift_item}. It has more use with you than sitting by my cauldron.
Take {gift_item}. It is not much, but it is given with care.
Good. {gift_item} sat well with {tested_villager}, like softened leather.
Then the fit was comfortable. {tested_villager} liked {gift_item}.
Good. {gift_item} suited {tested_villager}; I like advice that holds up.

{gift_item} rubbed wrong? Bring {alternative_gift}; better fit, less complaint.

That advice chafed. {alternative_gift} should sit easier.
Set {gift_item} aside and try {alternative_gift}. This advice should land better.
Then we correct the guess: {alternative_gift} next time.

Mind the tannery. What do you need?
Step clear of the tannery. What do you need?
Mind the tannery; I am listening.
Back to curing leather without wasting hide, then.
Back to leatherwork before the work notices I stopped.
I have stitch to tend and daylight to spend.
Fine. I will stitch this shut for now.
Fine. I will set this down before it gets heavier.
Fine. I can step back, but do not make me regret it.
That is not enough to mend it. Bring {emerald_cost} {emeralds}.
That is short of the full repair. Bring {emerald_cost} {emeralds}.
Not enough. It takes {emerald_cost} {emeralds} to settle this.
No. This split runs too deep for {payment_items}.
No. Some damage has to cool before payment matters. {payment_items}
No. Keep {payment_items}; trust is not ready to trade.
